institution_or_repository: Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres / Fondation Garnier
evidence: Académie approves 8,000 francs to Sylvain Lévi specifically to allow him to continue research on Buddhism in the sub-Himalayan regions.
implication: The 1897-98 mission interruption was not a generic absence: Buddhist research was an explicit funded objective immediately before Lovejoy's Paris year.

evidence: Barth reports Lévi arrived at Kathmandu in January 1898, had already located rare manuscripts, arranged acquisition/copying, and taken inscriptions.
implication: Fixes the Buddhist/Sanskrit manuscript-collection phase of the mission during the academic year in which Lévi taught no EPHE conference.

evidence: Senart reports Lévi's Nepal stay ending with acquisition of Asanga's Sūtrālaṅkāra manuscript, expected to provide a basis for future Mahāyāna research.
implication: Shows the mission generated concrete Mahāyāna textual materials immediately before Lévi's return to teaching.

evidence: Official report says Lévi, on mission in India, could conduct no conference during 1897-98; Finot maintained Sanskrit teaching.
implication: The Buddhist mission directly coincides with a full academic-year break in Lévi's regular EPHE instruction.

evidence: Corrected course poster preserves printed spring-1898 state naming Alfred Foucher as 'remplaçant' under Sylvain Lévi's Sanskrit chair; Foucher block includes holy cities/pilgrimages of Hinduism and is later cancelled in correction state.
implication: Direct institutional witness that Foucher covered Lévi's Collège chair during the mission.

evidence: EPHE annuaire records Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot representing the École pratique at the Abel Bergaigne monument inauguration at Vimy.
implication: Hard proof Lévi was back in France and active in the EPHE network by 9 Oct 1898.

evidence: Earliest Paris letter cited by Daniel J. Wilson for Lovejoy's Lévi/Vernes/Réville reconstruction.
implication: Only eight days after Lévi's hard Vimy presence anchor; exact letter wording still unrecovered.

evidence: Official programme says IVe Section conferences for 1898-99 begin 3 Nov 1898 at Nouvelle-Sorbonne, 46 rue Saint-Jacques.
implication: Provides precise institutional opening date for the Sanskrit/Indianist EPHE teaching cycle.

evidence: Faculty meeting explicitly processes current-year substitutes but contains no Lévi/Foucher pair and no Lévi/mission/Sanskrit/Pāli reference.
implication: Bounded negative becomes stronger when read alongside poster cancellation: Foucher was no longer being processed as continuing substitute.

institution_or_repository: Collège de France / corrected course poster
evidence: Working correction copy changes spring-1898 opening date to 5 December for first semester 1898-99 and cancels Foucher's replacement state under Lévi's chair.
implication: Collège teaching transition reaches a concrete opening-day marker exactly within Wilson's 1 Dec / 5 Dec Lovejoy letter window.

evidence: Lévi's regular conferences after return are Bhagavad-Gītā and continuous survey of Indian literature; no regular Pāli-Buddhism course appears in recovered report.
implication: Independent institutional corroboration of the reported unavailability of Lovejoy's desired Pāli-Buddhist study, while private readings remain letter-dependent.

evidence: Lévi formally reports to the Académie on the India/Japan mission; the Academy president congratulates him on its success.
implication: Closes the public administrative mission cycle after Lévi has resumed Paris teaching.

evidence: Published mission report identifies Ministry mission to India/Japan and additional Académie subsidy specifically for research in the target regions.
implication: Provides Lévi's own retrospective public account of the mission as a distinct documentary layer from course administration and Lovejoy's private study.
